issues.title: V0.23.0: Optimization of TPOT under low concurrency conditions
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR backports a stack of 10 performance / bugfix commits onto `releases/v0.23.0` that
significantly reduce decode TPOT for MoE models at low concurrency. All changes were
developed and validated on Atlas 910C (Ascend 910_93, CANN 9.1.0) with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
(TP=2), covering both plain decode and MTP speculative decoding.

Use case: latency-sensitive online serving (e.g. customer-service chat) where
single-digit-concurrency TPOT dominates user experience. On this workload the stack cuts
c=1 TPOT from ~8.2ms to ~7.6ms without MTP, and from ~7.0ms to ~5.1ms (-27%) with
MTP (num_speculative_tokens=4, min_tokens=512).

The stack, commit by commit:

1. **[Perf][Compilation] Add `enable_super_kernel` option for small-operator fusion**
   New `ascend_compilation_config` key `enable_super_kernel`; when set, passes
   `super_kernel_optimize` to the npugraph_ex compiler backend so small operators inside
   static kernels are fused automatically.

2. **[Perf][Kernel] Lower MoE weight prefetch token threshold to 1**
   `MOE_PREFETCH_TOKEN_THRESHOLD` 96 → 1 so MoE weight prefetch also stays active for
   small decode batches (previously skipped below 96 tokens), improving TPOT at
   concurrency 1/4/8 when `weight_prefetch_config` is enabled.

3. **[Perf][Compilation] Always enable SuperKernel optimization with static kernel**
   Enables `super_kernel_optimize` unconditionally whenever static kernel compilation is
   on (CANN 9.1+), letting the compiler apply SuperKernel stream fusion for
   compute-communication overlap; also adds it to the compiler cache hash factors.

4. **[Perf][Kernel] Overlap shared experts with routed experts and reduce decode overhead**
   - Runs shared experts on a side stream concurrently with routed experts when
     `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` is enabled; the shared-expert AllReduce stays on
     the side stream so it overlaps with routed expert computation.
   - Allows `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FUSED_MC2` and `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` to
     coexist (removes the previous mutual-exclusion check).
   - Skips dispatch/combine/gmm2 event recording in the overlap path via a new
     `skip_dispatch_combine_events` forward-context attribute.
   - Caches `(1.0 + weight)` for Gemma-style RMSNorm and the Qwen3.5 q/k norm patch
     instead of recomputing it every step.
   - Prefetches the next-layer shared-expert gate_up weight together with the routed
     gate_up weight so it lands in cache during the current layer's GroupedMatmul.

5. **[Perf][ModelRunner] Reduce per-step kernel launches and host overhead for decode**
   - GDN: caches the transposed contiguous conv1d weight (saves one
     `aclnnContiguous_Transpose` launch per layer per step); cat-free
     `rearrange_mixed_qkv` returning reshape views for single-token decode; fused q/k
     L2Norm into a single call for single-token decode.
   - Sampler: greedy fast path that skips the bf16→fp32 cast and returns int32 token ids
     directly (argmax ordering is preserved since every bf16 value is exactly
     representable in fp32).
   - Model runner: overlaps the mamba align-mode state copy with `update_cos_sin` on the
     global stream; skips redundant `commit_block_table` / `copy_to_gpu` / `fill_` calls
     when batch shape and block-table contents are unchanged; copies positions from the
     pinned CPU buffer instead of recomputing on device.
   - Block table: CPU fast path for slot-mapping on small decode batches (avoids the
     fixed triton kernel launch overhead); pinned staging buffer reuse in
     `commit_block_table` and `copy_snapshot_to_gpu`.
   - Rotary embedding: single `index_select` shared by cos and sin.

6. **[Perf][ModelRunner] Skip full-vocab all-gather for greedy decode via vocab-parallel argmax**
   Greedy fast path in `execute_model`: when the whole batch is greedy with no
   logprobs/penalties/masks/structured-output/spec-decode, a vocab-parallel argmax is
   computed instead of materializing full-vocab logits — each TP rank computes its local
   argmax and only `(value, index)` pairs are all-gathered, dropping sampling
   communication from O(batch × vocab_size) to O(batch × 2 × tp_size) (e.g. 248KB → 8B
   per rank for a 248K vocab at TP=2). Pre-sampled ids are carried in
   `ExecuteModelState` and turned directly into a `SamplerOutput`.

7. **[Perf][ModelRunner] Harden greedy vocab-parallel argmax fast path**
   Resolves the logits processor through `model.language_model` for wrapper/multimodal
   models; extracts the MinTokens EOS mask from the active logits processor; skips the
   redundant `.to(torch.int32)` cast; guards accepted-token event recording with
   `speculative_config is not None`; reuses a pre-allocated NPU event for the mamba
   align-mode stream sync (removes per-step event create/destroy, ~10µs host each step);
   AllReduce+RMSNorm fusion pass enabled for all compile ranges including decode.

8. **[BugFix][Kernel] Make multistream shared-expert overlap capture-safe for MTP**
   The side-stream overlap path was not capture-safe: during NPU graph capture the
   shared-experts side stream is not registered with the graph pool, so any side-stream
   op — or even a `wait_stream()` recording an event on it — fails with
   `aclrtAllocatorGetByStream` / `rtStreamWaitEvent` errors, crashing startup at graph
   capture when MTP is combined with the overlap. All side-stream usage is now gated
   behind `not capturing`: capture records the serial default-stream path, while the
   overlap runs in eager warmup and at replay time.

9. **[Perf][Sample] Cache min_tokens EOS mask for spec-decode rejection sampling**
   `MinTokensLogitsProcessor.apply_with_spec_decode` rebuilds the `(row, token)` EOS mask
   on the host and copies it H2D from *pageable* memory every step, serializing the async
   scheduling pipeline (measured ~30% of step time at c=1 with MTP). The new
   `_apply_min_tokens_spec_cached` caches the device tensors during the steady phase
   (remaining min_tokens ≥ num_draft_tokens) so each step issues a single `index_put_`;
   rebuilds go through pinned memory on batch-structure change, and requests near the
   min_tokens tail fall back to the upstream implementation (semantics identical).
   Also adds `_vocab_parallel_argmax_eos_masked`, a local vocab-parallel greedy argmax
   with shard-local EOS masking, removing the dependency on a non-upstream
   `get_top_tokens` signature; the fast path safely falls back to full logits when an
   unsupported argmax-changing processor is present.
   Reworks the AllReduce+RMSNorm fusion pattern to match the actual vLLM 0.23 decode
   graph (2-arg `unquantized_gemm`, copy/detach of the o_proj output, inline Gemma-style
   `weight + 1.0`, 3-arg `npu_add_rms_norm_bias`).

10. **[Perf][ModelRunner] Vocab-parallel argmax for greedy spec-decode verification**
    Extends the vocab-parallel argmax to MTP verification: `_spec_greedy_shard_argmax`
    computes the lm_head shard locally, applies the steady-state MinTokens EOS mask on
    the shard, and all-gathers only `(value, index)` pairs for all selected rows (target
    draft rows + bonus rows); `AscendRejectionSampler.forward_greedy_presampled` runs the
    greedy rejection kernels directly on the pre-sampled ids, skipping the full-vocab
    logits all-gather, fp32 materialization and clone. Mask indices are pre-filtered to
    the local vocab shard on the host at cache-build time, so per-step masking is pure
    integer indexing — boolean-mask indexing (`masked_select` → NonZero on Ascend) forces
    a host-device sync worth several ms per step in the async pipeline.
    Can be disabled with `VLLM_ASCEND_DISABLE_SPEC_GREEDY_FAST=1`.

Safety: every greedy fast path is strictly condition-guarded (all-greedy batch, no
logprobs, no penalties, no allowed/bad-word masks, no unsupported logits processors, no
grammar, steady-phase min_tokens only) and falls back to the original full-logits path
otherwise, so sampling semantics are unchanged whenever a fast path does not apply.

Measured on Atlas 910C, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP=2, FULL_DECODE_ONLY cudagraph, static kernel
+ AllReduce/RMSNorm fusion + fused MC2:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| c=1 TPOT (no MTP) | ~8.2 ms | ~7.6 ms |
| c=1 TPOT (MTP=4, min_tokens=512) | ~7.0 ms | ~5.1 ms (-27%) |
| c=4 TPOT (MTP=4, min_tokens=512) | ~8.9 ms | ~9.0 ms (unchanged) |
| c=8 TPOT (MTP=4, min_tokens=512) | ~12.7 ms | ~12.4 ms |

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes — all changes are opt-in or backward compatible:

- New `ascend_compilation_config` key: `enable_super_kernel` (commit 1); in the final
  state `super_kernel_optimize` is enabled automatically whenever
  `enable_static_kernel`/npugraph_ex static kernel compilation is on (commit 3).
- `MOE_PREFETCH_TOKEN_THRESHOLD` default lowered 96 → 1; only takes effect when
  `weight_prefetch_config` is enabled.
- `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` can now coexist with `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FUSED_MC2`
  (the previous mutual-exclusion auto-disable is removed) and with MTP graph capture
  (capture-safe gating).
- New env var `VLLM_ASCEND_DISABLE_SPEC_GREEDY_FAST=1` to disable the spec-decode greedy
  vocab-parallel argmax fast path.
- The AllReduce+RMSNorm fusion pass now applies to all compile ranges (including decode)
  when `fuse_allreduce_rms` is enabled.
- Greedy decode/spec-decode fast paths only trigger for all-greedy batches without
  logprobs/penalties/masks/structured outputs; in every other case behavior is identical
  to before.

### How was this patch tested?

Tested on Atlas 910C (Ascend 910_93, CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0,
vLLM 0.23.0):

1. **Build**: installed from source with `pip install -e . --no-build-isolation`; all
   csrc custom ops compile cleanly for `ascend910_93`.

2. **Server startup** (covers static-kernel/SuperKernel compilation and full-graph
   capture):

```bash
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export LOCAL_WORLD_SIZE=2
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export ACLNN_CACHE_LIMIT=100000
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FUSED_MC2=1
export HCCL_DETERMINISTIC=false
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=128
vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
  --served-model-name dewu-chat \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5001 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.82 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 20, 40, 80]}' \
  --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"enable_static_kernel": true, "fuse_allreduce_rms": true, "enable_super_kernel": true}}' \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --seed 42
```

   Static kernel compilation, SuperKernel optimization and cudagraph capture complete
   successfully; `Application startup complete` with no errors in the log.

3. **Functional check**: `/v1/chat/completions` requests with up to 1k-token Chinese
   prompts (`max_tokens` 180–256) return coherent, on-topic completions; usage counters
   are consistent.

4. **Determinism check**: two identical requests at `temperature=0` produce
   byte-identical outputs (md5 match), confirming the greedy fast paths do not perturb
   sampling results.

5. **Performance check**: c=1 end-to-end decode ≈ 8.6 ms/token for this configuration
   (in line with the ~8 ms class measured for the non-MTP path); MTP + min_tokens
   scenarios were benchmarked separately with the numbers in the table above (MTP
   acceptance rate unchanged at 0.68, TTFT ~195ms).

6. **MTP capture-safety check** (commit 8): with
   `additional_config.multistream_overlap_shared_expert=true` and MTP
   (`num_speculative_tokens=4`), both PIECEWISE and FULL capture complete and the server
   serves correct completions (previously crashed at capture start).

No new unit tests are included in this PR: the changes are NPU-runtime/graph-capture and
host-scheduling-pipeline specific (side-stream capture safety, static-kernel compiler
options, HCCL communication patterns, pinned-memory/async-scheduling timing), which
cannot be exercised on CPU-only CI runners; correctness was validated end-to-end on
910C hardware as described above, and every fast path falls back to the pre-existing
code path when its guard conditions are not met. Happy to add e2e nightly cases
following the `tests/e2e` configuration if maintainers prefer.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change involves
  boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max values,
  off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable, I
  added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or `tests/e2e/`.
  Edge cases are handled in code by construction (single-token-decode-only view/fusion
  paths, min_tokens tail fallback, stale batch-index fallback, grammar fallback,
  TP=1 early return, empty-mask short circuits), but the behaviors require NPU runtime
  and cannot be unit-tested on CPU CI — see "How was this patch tested?".
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression test
  that would fail without the fix.
  The capture-safety fix (commit 8) only reproduces during NPU graph capture with MTP +
  multistream overlap enabled; it is validated by server startup on 910C rather than a
  CI-runnable test.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths (exceptions,
  timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
  All fast paths fall back to the original full-logits/serial paths when their guard
  conditions are not met (non-greedy batch, logprobs, penalties, token masks, grammar,
  unsupported logits processors, min_tokens tail, batch-structure change, capture time).
- [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [x] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.
  Benchmark results attached above (c=1 TPOT 8.2→7.6ms without MTP; 7.0→5.1ms with
  MTP=4 + min_tokens=512; c=4/c=8 unchanged or improved). No automated perf-regression
  test added — requires Atlas 910C hardware.

issues.title: [Feature] Add 910C matmul-allreduce-rmsnorm fusion op for Qwen3 down-projection
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds a **fused matmul + allreduce + add + rmsnorm operator targeting Ascend 910C**, specialized for the **Qwen3 down-projection** path, and wires it through the vllm-ascend compilation graph-fusion layer.

**Background — different swim-lanes, converged onto this release.**
This fusion work was developed on a separate internal development branch (different "swim-lane" from the mainline v0.22.1rc work). It is contributed here on top of the current `releases/v0.22.1rc` baseline so the three-operator fusion (matmul → allreduce → rmsnorm) lands as a single coherent change on this release rather than as scattered commits. The four original development commits (which included WIP staging) have been squashed into this one clean commit for review.

**Why fusion helps.**
The Qwen3 down-projection normally issues a matmul, then an allreduce, then a residual add and an rmsnorm as separate kernels. Each is a separate kernel launch plus, for the collective, a host-device round trip. Fusing the four stages into one 910C op removes those launches and round trips, reducing the down-projection latency.

**What this PR adds:**

- `csrc/mc2/matmul_allreduce_add_rmsnorm_910c/`: the aclnn host adapter (def/proto/tiling/workspace), the aclnn torch entry, the AIC and AIV kernels, tiling, utils, and shared `moe_distribute` base/comm-context helpers.
- `csrc/` wiring: `CMakeLists` entries, `func.cmake` registration, `torch_binding.cpp` / `torch_binding_meta.cpp` bindings, and `build.sh` / `build_aclnn.sh` entries.
- `vllm_ascend/compilation/passes/allreduce_rmsnorm_fusion_pass.py`: the graph fusion pass that matches the down-proj → allreduce → add → rmsnorm pattern and routes it to the new fused op on 910C.
- `vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py`, `compiler_interface.py`, `graph_fusion_pass_manager.py`, `passes/base_pattern.py`: config and base-pattern plumbing so the pass is registered and gated behind the Ascend compilation config.
- `tests/ut/compilation/test_compiler_interface.py`: unit tests for the fusion pass registration/matching.

**Implementation notes:**

- AIC/AIV scheduling uses a 1:1 ratio for the fused decode op; the matmul and the collective epilogue are pipelined to overlap compute and communication.
- The op is gated behind the 910C Ascend compilation config path; other hardware and non-Qwen3 paths are unaffected.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, opt-in. The fused op is registered behind the Ascend compilation config for 910C and is exercised via the allreduce_rmsnorm fusion pass. It activates for the Qwen3 down-projection path when the 910C compilation config enables it; existing paths and other hardware are unchanged. No public Python API name changes.

### How was this patch tested?

- `python3 -m py_compile` on all changed `.py` files (pass).
- `bash -n` on changed shell scripts `csrc/build.sh`, `csrc/build_aclnn.sh` (pass).
- `ruff check` on changed `.py` files (pass).
- `tests/ut/compilation/test_compiler_interface.py` is included for the fusion-pass registration/matching (CPU-runnable; CI to run).
- Full NPU correctness/latency validation for the fused op on 910C was performed on the originating development branch prior to this squash; CI verification of the release-baseline build and the new UT is requested here.

Cherry-picked and squashed from internal branch `codex/matmul-allreduce-rmsnorm-910c` (original commits 5d6f2514, 7cd0b513, 4fe895ec, 4cad84e4).

- vLLM version: v0.22.1
- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/967c5c3bc38891f4465d3f4e99917ed837bb3833

issues.title: [Ops][Feature] Add Ascend PLE INT8 table support for Qwen4Exp ModelSlim checkpoints
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Support Qwen4Exp PLE n-gram tables exported by ModelSlim as symmetric INT8 weights with one FP32 scale per 32 columns. Detect `INT8_SYM` markers, keep the table in INT8, load TP-local `shard_N.scale` rows, and dequantize only looked-up rows to the model dtype before TP AllReduce. Pinned-host PLE prefetch rejects this format explicitly.

The latest compatibility fix uses vLLM's embedding `_copy_embedding_shard_` method when available, while retaining the older module helper for v0.32.0. The current-vLLM INT8 PLE unit tests passed 3/3 without a runtime shim.

The latest fix accumulates scale shards across checkpoint-file loader calls and validates completeness after all weights load. The earlier per-call check rejected this real checkpoint because its scale shards are spread across multiple files. Duplicate shards across calls still fail. This is a model-loading fix, not a claimed fix for the intermittent D-side HCCL stall.

The documentation covers export, reconstruction, metadata, and conversion from an existing W8A8/MXFP8 checkpoint. This model-local Ascend patch should eventually move into upstream Qwen4Exp.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Release note fragment: `release_notes/fragments/20310.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

- Focused CPU unit tests: **3 passed** on 141.61.141.62, including a regression where the two required TP scale shards arrive in separate weight-file batches, final missing-shard validation, and cross-batch duplicate rejection.
- Local `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed. Local pytest could not run because the Windows environment has no `torch`; the same test file passed in the remote development environment.
- Real checkpoint: the INT8 PLE model loads on Ascend 950DT, a P/D proxy request succeeds, and model-loading memory is 47.63 GiB per card versus 58.07 GiB with the BF16 PLE table. The serving environment also contains the separate PyTorch PLE short-convolution adaptation, so these are integrated-runtime observations rather than an isolated test of this PR alone.
- GPQA Diamond, 32K maximum output, concurrency 32: a diagnostic INT8 P/D run completed 198/198 (165 correct); uninstrumented INT8 with D on NPU4–7 reproduced a D TP AllReduce jetty SQ overflow after 24 completed cases. Moving D to NPU0–3 completed 86 cases without overflow in a bounded run. The requested full 198-case swapped-device run stalled at 70 completed cases: D NPU2 (worker 366726) reported jetty SQ overflow on TP group_name_3 AllReduce at 18:44:49 CST, then generation throughput went to zero and shared-memory broadcast waited. The task-owned client was stopped after the confirmed stall (exit 143). This rules out a failure fixed solely by moving D away from NPU4; there is no valid full 198-case uninstrumented INT8 score. These observations do **not** establish a stable uninstrumented INT8 accuracy or resolve the intermittent HCCL stall.
- `format.sh ci` was unavailable locally because `pre-commit` is absent. Pinned-host operation is intentionally unsupported.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing
- [x] TP scale-shard boundary and split-file regression coverage.
- [x] Malformed, missing, and duplicate scale failure paths.
- [x] Focused real NPU model-load and proxy-request evidence.
- [ ] Resolve the D-side HCCL stall and complete comparable full accuracy/performance validation before merge.
- [ ] Required CI checks.

### Additional integrated P/D performance validation (2026-10-31)

The PR head is `50c2e9bd9345a0fc07fb317938fdf292fd0f0338`. The `ple_int8.py` and focused test Git blobs in the 8-card benchmark worktree match this head. The serving worktree also overlays PRs #20344, #20402 and, for the PP/SP run, #20311; these are integrated-runtime results, not isolated PR #20310 speedups.

- INT8 PLE checkpoint: `/mnt/share/weight/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-w8a8-mxfp8-ple-int8-g32-20261029`; 128 PLE `INT8_SYM` markers. Serving with P/D Prefix Cache disabled. Model-loading weight memory was 47.63 GiB/card versus 58.07 GiB/card with the original PLE tables (10.44 GiB/card lower); the fixed GPU memory utilization reallocates much of this space to KV Cache, so total runtime HBM does not fall by that amount.
- TP4+TP4 P/D, P MegaMoE off: AISBench 16K input / 1 output token, C1/N4 and C2/N8 completed 4/4 and 8/8 with zero failures. TTFT 1775.9 / 2791.9 ms; input throughput 9251.6582 / 11144.5106 token/s. P prompt-token deltas 65739 / 131479.
- PP2×TP2 P with SP and MegaMoE EP2, PP1×TP2×DP2 D with SP, after adding #20311: 16K/1 C1/N4 and C2/N8 completed 4/4 and 8/8. TTFT 1556.8 / 1975.7 ms; input throughput 10553.8192 / 15802.4033 token/s. CANN MegaMoE EP-world=2 allocation and FlashComm1 enablement were observed in P logs; D finished FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph capture.
- Same PP/SP P/D: 131072-target input / 1 output token, actual chat input 131123–131124 tokens. C1/N4 and C2/N8 completed 4/4 and 8/8, zero failures. TTFT 9908.1 / 16615.5 ms; input throughput 13231.2665 / 14840.3433 token/s. P prompt-token deltas 524491 / 1048983. Both cache resets returned HTTP 200; P, D, and proxy remained healthy after testing.

Client TTFT includes proxy and D handoff. With one output token, TPOT is not meaningful. This evidence does not resolve the separate intermittent D-side HCCL/GPQA issue described above.
